title: LLM inference serving, Part 2: the KV cache
tldr: What the KV cache stores, how big it gets, and why it, not compute, caps how many requests one GPU can serve: why attention's keys and values can be stored and what skipping the cache costs, how one request's cache fills across prefill and decode, MHA vs MQA vs GQA, the bytes-per-token formula worked for Llama 3.1 8B and 70B, how vLLM v0.31.0 sizes the cache pool with gpu_memory_utilization, a KV sizing calculator and a tested estimator, why decode must also read every request's cache and stays memory-bound at long contexts, what breaks when the cache fills, where the Redis-session analogy breaks, and an interview drill.
